Ṛgvidhāna
on the use of various mantras of Ṛv. for japa for attaining diverse ends. by Śaunaka. There are a. least three texts, two qualified a. Bṛhad or Jyeṣṭha an. Laghu or Samkṣipta an. a third in 4 chs., with a short fifth added in some mss. There is a text called Ṛv. kārikā which appears to carry the former text with additional verses on Ṛṣi, Chandas an. Devatā of Ṛks. dealt with in Ṛgvidhāna; sometimes a ms. simply called Ṛgvidhāna has these verses, C.. MD. 884. MD. 14782, called Ṛṣidevatā-cchandovivaraṇa, is really Ṛgvidhāna with these indications. C.. I. 34, though agreeing with Jyeṣṭha or Bṛhad is called Laghu. Among these texts Mantrapratīkas an. phala or uses are generally common, but actually identical verses are only a few. Some mss. give the indications of Ṛv. Aṣṭaka an. Adhyāya (e.g. GD. 11. MD. 884). MD. 884, some verses of which agree with one version, some others with another (that in 4 or 5 chs.), has a unique sup. called Uttarakalpa giving mantras an. their prescription for various ailments an. finishes with a stotra on Devī in ten verses. Some mss. give a small number of verses within hundred but the numbering here which is irregular is no indication of a short text.
